title: Last 24: The day the sky fell
author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
selftext:
I'm developing a merge game about the 11 September attacks. Seems weird and creepy, but works well and has a very good story imo, with many playable subvariants, it's my main focus. I'm creating and writing the story and texts 100%, AI is creating the rest. It's in very early development.

Someone wants to try it from 11 September 2026 to ahead and give feedback?

I have the game in portuguese (my native language) and english (translated with AI).

Besides that, I want to know too if Gymnopedie nº1 is yet copyright music and if I need to remove it totally or not before sharing.  
I will improve the graphics when I finish the total structure, but I'm focusing in putting the playable ideas before.

comments.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
comments.body:
This was to be a book (is in advanced phase in that matter, with 1 prologue + 27 moments fro 22 wars+ 1 epilogue for 22 ways + 3 dreams for evey way already written), after was to be an interactive fiction. Finally I'm transforming it in a game.  
Are +-700 different text pages already written.

comments.author: st0cktalk
comments.body: So here's my feedback. Right now, it doesn't really seem that interesting. It seems more like a, well, what we call a fetch quest, which, if you're not familiar with, is just sort of a process where you go and get an item and then come back with it and then go and get an item and come back with it. And while developers have tried to make that interesting, fetch quests have a stigma around them within the gaming community. What I might do is if you want to make it more of an interactive fiction, don't lay out all the story at once. I think part of the reason why I don't find this very attractive right now is because there are so many different choices and so many things to do. I can definitely see potential here, but right now I just don't see this as a very fun-looking game. If you have questions, feel free to respond. I'm happy to give you more feedback if you'd like. The direction I can see you taking this is where each item becomes something exciting for the player to find. Sort of like finding a new ability in Castlevania, or any Metroidvania, really, that allows you to do a new part of the story. So it requires writing the story well, of course, to motivate this, because this is also something that has been done a lot. But I feel like it's a little bit more attractive to strive for a single goal than to have a huge branch of stories laid out.

replies.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
replies.body: Of course. Thanks for feedback. I would be grateful for more ways to improve it, maybe changing totally the game focus can be a good solution. The story is very deep already, I think cutting it wouldn't be a good solution, much time spent too. I never played Castlevania/Metroidvania, but I think you are talking about something similar to RPG's like Pokemon. Correct me if I'm wrong. So, I need to develop a map, do you agree? Maybe a double map with simplified floors of Twin Towers by one side and NY city by the other. What do you suggest me in that field? What do you have in mind. I'm not experienced as a videogame creator. I focused more in story. Only recently with vibe coding I started to do it. But I see some potential in my idea. I don't know simply how to put it in practice in the perfect way.

replies.author: st0cktalk
replies.body: You misunderstand. I'm not saying to cut your story. I'm saying the story should not be completely available at the start. So have them start from a central point, and then only when they receive the item, right, by succeeding at the interaction or by figuring out the clues to gain that item, will they be able to unlock the next part of the story. So the UI would need to change, because right now we can see everything. We can see all the stories. I would be paralyzed with that amount of choice. I'm saying a single choice in the beginning, and then you can add your story as it progresses. And that needs to be reflected visually.

replies.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
replies.body: No, we can't see all stories, this is only the first 9 parts of the story, in early day 10, the story is much bigger than this. You have the dream phase (in the 10 September night), you have the card phase (where the tarot fate card is played), you have the evacuation of Twin towers (in some scenarios), you have even the post Twin Towers collapse with the survivors that resist and the story that happens after 2001 until 2026.

replies.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
replies.body:
And you can only open and read the 8 first following parts of the story after concluding the before part.  
You can't read the chapter 3 until finish chapter 1 and 2.

replies.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
replies.body:
You have the canonical storyline, and then it begins to diverge wildly depending on which quests you prioritize completing, ultimately leading to a specific Destiny Card.

We even have one scenario in which the protagonist manages to save everyone who would have been inside the towers by discovering in advance what is going to happen, allowing both towers to be completely evacuated.

At the opposite extreme, there are scenarios in which the tower collapses immediately and nobody survives.
